corruptions.text:
FINDING: The largest known example of European Iron Age silver work is the Gundestrup cauldron, which originated from Denmark.

This cauldron dates from between 200 BC and 300 AD, or more narrowly between 150 BC and 1 BC, placing it within the late La Tène period or early Roman Iron Age. It measures 69 cm in diameter and 42 cm in height, making it the largest known example of European Iron Age silver work.
